kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-02.title: Diagonal of the square of centres
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-02.body:
The centres of the four big circles form a square of side 2 (neighbouring circles touch). Its diagonal is $2\sqrt2$. Along the diagonal we pass radius 1, the small circle's diameter $2r$, and radius 1: $1 + 2r + 1 = 2\sqrt2$, so $r = \sqrt2 - 1$.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-02.title: Distance to the centre
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-02.body:
The small circle is centred at the centre of the square of centres. The distance from there to a big circle's centre is half the diagonal, $\sqrt2$, and must equal $1 + r$. So $r = \sqrt2 - 1 \approx 0.41$.

**Answer: (A)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-03.title: Count neighbouring faces
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-03.body:
Each of the 12 sides of the 12-gon is an edge shared with another face. Two different faces of a polyhedron cannot share two edges along the 12-gon (two adjacent faces meet in a single edge), so there are at least 12 further faces: at least $1 + 12 = 13$ faces.

A pyramid over a 12-gon has exactly 13 faces (the base and 12 triangles), so 13 is possible.

**Answer: (B) 13**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-11.title: A kite of two right triangles
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-11.body:
Take side length 1 and let $O$ be the common vertex. The overlap is a kite $OPQR$: $OR$ is a side of the upright square, $OP$ a side of the tilted square (both of length 1), and $Q$ is where the two other sides cross. The angles at $P$ and $R$ are right angles (corners of the squares), so the kite consists of two congruent right triangles $OPQ$ and $ORQ$ with hypotenuse $OQ$.

The angle $\angle ROP = 45^\circ$ is bisected by $OQ$, so $RQ = \tan 22.5^\circ = \sqrt2 - 1$. Area of the kite $= 2\cdot\frac12\cdot 1\cdot(\sqrt2 - 1) = \sqrt2 - 1$, and this is also the fraction of the square's area.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-11.title: Coordinates
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-11.body:
Put $O = (0,0)$, the upright square $[0,1]\times[0,1]$, and the tilted square with sides along $y = x$ and $y = -x$ from $O$ (side 1, so its right corner is $P = (\frac{1}{\sqrt2}, \frac{1}{\sqrt2})$). Its far side $y = -x + \sqrt2$ meets $y = 1$ at $Q = (\sqrt2 - 1, 1)$. The overlap is the quadrilateral $O, P, Q, R = (0,1)$. With $a = \frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $b = \sqrt2 - 1$ the shoelace formula gives

$$\text{Area} = \tfrac12\left(a\cdot 1 - b\cdot a + b\cdot 1\right) = \tfrac12\left(a(1 - b) + b\right) = \tfrac12\left((\sqrt2 - 1) + (\sqrt2 - 1)\right) = \sqrt2 - 1,$$

using $a(1-b) = \frac{2 - \sqrt2}{\sqrt2} = \sqrt2 - 1$.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-18.title: Factor
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-18.body:
$(x - y)(x + y) = 84$. The two factors have the same parity (their sum is $2x$), and their product is even, so both are even: $(x-y, x+y) \in \{(2, 42), (6, 14)\}$ (with $x - y < x + y$ and $y > 0$).

- $(2, 42)$: $x = 22$, $y = 20$, $x^2 + y^2 = 884$.
- $(6, 14)$: $x = 10$, $y = 4$, $x^2 + y^2 = 116$.

Two values.

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-18.title: Halve the factors
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-18.body:
Write $x - y = 2u$, $x + y = 2v$; then $uv = 21$ with $u < v$: $(1, 21)$ or $(3, 7)$. Each gives one pair $(x, y) = (u+v, v-u)$, namely $(22, 20)$ and $(10, 4)$, with different values of $x^2 + y^2$ ($884$ and $116$).

**Answer: (B) 2**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-22.title: Shift into the interval
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-22.body:
$2013 = 5\cdot 403 - 2$, so by periodicity $f(2013) = f(-2)$, and $-2$ lies in $[-2, 3)$: $f(-2) = 4$.

(Careful: $2013 \equiv 3 \pmod 5$, but $3$ is *not* in $[-2, 3)$, so we must use $-2$ instead of $3$ — the answer is not 9.)

**Answer: (D) 4**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-23.title: Count face by face
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-23.body:
$2013 = 3\cdot 11\cdot 61$, so (taking a genuinely three-dimensional prism) the dimensions are $3\times 11\times 61$. All dimensions are odd, so with a black cube in one corner, all eight corners are black, and every face is an odd $\times$ odd chessboard with black corners. Such an $m\times n$ board has $\frac{mn + 1}{2}$ black squares.

- Two $3\times 11$ faces: $2\cdot 17 = 34$
- Two $3\times 61$ faces: $2\cdot 92 = 184$
- Two $11\times 61$ faces: $2\cdot 336 = 672$

Total $34 + 184 + 672 = 890$.

**Answer: (C) 890**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-25.title: Add up angles
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-25.body:
Let $T$ be the number of triangles. Their angles add up to $180^\circ\cdot T$. On the other hand, the angles around each of the 2013 inner points add up to $360^\circ$, and the angles at the four corners of the square add up to $4\cdot 90^\circ = 360^\circ$. So

$$180T = 360\cdot 2013 + 360 \implies T = 2\cdot 2013 + 2 = 4028.$$

**Answer: (D) 4028**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-25.title: Add points one at a time
kangaroo-ca-2013-g1112-25.body:
With no inner points, a diagonal splits the square into 2 triangles. Adding an inner point inside a triangle splits it into 3 (net $+2$); one on a common edge splits two triangles into four (also net $+2$). So $n$ points give $2n + 2$ triangles: $4028$.

**Answer: (D) 4028**
